items.headline: Cursor capitalizes on GitHub frustration, launches rival hosting platform
items.facts: Cursor launched Origin, a new code‑hosting platform to compete with GitHub.

framing.publicBrief: Developer frustration with GitHub has opened a window for competition. Cursor has launched Origin, a new code-hosting platform designed to challenge GitHub’s dominance. The move targets developers seeking alternatives, aiming to capture market share by offering a rival infrastructure for code storage and collaboration. The industry watches to see if Origin can sustain a foothold against the established standard.

roleFlavor.contributor: You represent the development community deciding whether to migrate workflows to the new platform or remain with the incumbent.

howItWorks: The community decides collectively whether to adopt the new platform.
GitHub retains its existing network of users and repositories.
Cursor must attract enough developers to make Origin viable.
The outcome depends on the level of migration from the incumbent.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Will the community migrate to Origin?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Origin gains critical mass and challenges GitHub.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: Developers stay with GitHub; Origin fails to launch effectively.
outcomes.MIXED: A split market emerges with limited adoption on both sides.
